method: Flesch Kincaid grade plus five, using a vowel-group syllable heuristic. Punctuated sentences and standalone task lines are counted as sentence units. Exact corpora and hashes retained. Quantity table fragments, headings, staff text, dates, lesson codes and the verbatim scheme outcome are excluded. Estimates guide editing; they are not learner assessments. Read-aloud and confirmed scribing routes are available.

Use these invented classroom values to practise. They are not supplier prices or actual cash spending. Your own sheet must say actual agreed allocation or estimate.
30p + 15p = 45p = £0.45 materials cost. A 60p budget would have 15p left. Labour, tools and overheads are unpriced; this is not the full business cost.
The 210 mm by 297 mm sheet holds the 120 mm by 260 mm body in a 120 mm strip. In the remaining 90 mm strip, the channel can rotate to 30 mm by 100 mm and the 80 mm by 60 mm test card fits below it. Charge the whole sheet once, including offcuts and test card.
The model issues three 10 cm lengths, totalling 30 cm. This allowance includes offcuts. It does not claim a pupil measured or used exactly 30 cm.
A retained Week 2 mock-up is not recharged every week. If another trial used a separately allocated sheet or tape, include that allocation once with the real recorded waste. Different materials need their own adult-agreed invented values.
In your book, use one row per agreed resource allocation. Mark actual allocation / estimate ___. Date ___. Product or planned design ___. Adult-agreed price source ___. No shop research is required.
My materials total is ___ p = £___. One calculation I can explain ___. Planned allocation ___. Actual allocation or estimate ___. What changed ___. Its cost effect ___. Support used ___.
[ ] Keep planned, actual allocation and estimate separate. Name the quantity unit and invented unit price.
[ ] Charge the issued sheet once. Do not add the body, channel, test card or offcuts again. Do not recharge a retained Week 2 mock-up each week.
[ ] Record actual issued 10 cm tape portions if known. An unknown allowance is an estimate, not a measurement.
[ ] Add only a real allocated change. One extra 10 cm tape length adds 5p: 45p becomes 50p.
[ ] The model covers materials only. Labour, tools and overheads are unpriced, so this is not a full business cost.

Plan 120 seconds. Use your own words about the actual work, or clearly label a planned-product estimate. Present privately to an adult or use an agreed accessible mode. You do not need a public audience, video or physical item.

The printed card totals 120 seconds; it does not prove the talk happened or lasted that long. A prepared script alone is planning evidence. Record the real duration and accessible support.

Look across five weeks and six outcome rows. Use real work. You may speak, sign, point to records or confirm a scribe’s words. Keep your own judgement.

A tick or reflection records lesson evidence. It does not certify completion of the unit award. Missing practical evidence remains missing until it is actually collected.

Finish your cost, talk record and review first. This is a model. No sale or price search is needed.
45p is above materials cost. Labour, tools and overheads have no price in this model. The difference is not net profit. An asking price does not prove a sale.
One more issued 10 cm tape piece adds 5p. The model materials cost becomes 50p. At a 90p asking price, 40p is above materials cost before other costs. This is a model unless the extra tape was really issued.
A 60p materials budget minus 45p leaves 15p in that budget. This is different from 90p asking price minus 45p materials cost.
My comparison uses an actual allocation / estimate / model ___. One cost not priced ___. Why I cannot call the difference net profit ___. One further question ___.
Only add the 5p finish-paper piece if it was issued. Otherwise label it as an idea. It is not in the 45p model total.

This is a review lesson. No new cutting, joining or powered or heated tool is required. A safe, accessible explanation can use a drawing, a record or own words.
1 Today is costing, presentation and review. No cutting or new tool work is required. Keep tools returned and the work area clear.
2 The adult checks a real item before handling or showing it. Do not handle damaged or suspect edges. Use a drawing or actual record if the item is not safe or available.
3 Present privately to an adult or use an agreed accessible mode. No forced public display, peer audience, video or personal disclosure.
4 Any photo is object only with no people, names or identifying background. Do not upload work or private records through the lesson page.
5 A printed two-minute card is a plan. Record the real observed mode, duration and help; do not invent a presentation or earlier practical evidence.
Tell the adult. Use only an actual available record or a labelled model. Keep practical gaps visible. Do not handle an unsafe item or recreate earlier evidence as though it happened before.
With no product, tools, paper, printer or device, hear the model prices. Use spoken sums and label your cost as an estimate. You may give a real private talk if an adult sees or hears it. Keep the actual mode, time and help. Use real work in your review, or name each gap. An adult can write your words and read them back. If no record can yet be made, the written record stays pending. Missing making, tests and actual product cost stay pending.
Type instead starts closed and exports a local text file. Keep private health records and personal details out of response boxes.
